description:
Multiple public structs in pkix-ct expose Vec-typed fields directly:

- pkix-ct/src/sct.rs:138 — \`pub struct SctList(pub Vec<SignedCertificateTimestamp>);\`
- pkix-ct/src/sct.rs:72 — \`pub extensions: Vec<u8>\` on SignedCertificateTimestamp
- pkix-ct/src/sct.rs:82 — \`pub signature: Vec<u8>\` on SignedCertificateTimestamp
- pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:582 — \`pub signature: alloc::vec::Vec<u8>\` on SignedTreeHead
- pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:602 — \`pub audit_path: alloc::vec::Vec<[u8; 32]>\` on MerkleAuditPath
- pkix-ct/src/log_list.rs:34 — \`pub key_der: Vec<u8>\` on CtLog

What callers cannot depend on / what locks in: every consumer pattern-matching or constructing these structs binds to \`Vec<_>\` specifically. The maintainer can never switch to \`Box<[_]>\` (no realloc/capacity overhead, smaller stack footprint), \`SmallVec<[_; 4]>\` (typical SCT lists are 2-3 entries; stack-allocated would avoid an alloc per cert), \`Cow<'a, [_]>\` (zero-copy parsing path), or any \`AsRef<[_]>\`-shaped type, without a breaking change.

Distinct from PKIX-q74z.7 (\`#[non_exhaustive]\`): that finding addresses adding fields/variants. This addresses changing existing field TYPES. Adding \`#[non_exhaustive]\` does not let you change \`pub signature: Vec<u8>\` to \`pub signature: Box<[u8]>\` non-breakingly.

Distinct from PKIX-q74z.8 (CtLogList derive ergonomics): that's about derive bounds; this is about field-type lock-in on the parsed wire types.

Fix shape: either keep fields private and expose accessor methods returning \`&[T]\` / \`impl AsRef<[T]>\`, or accept that 0.x → 1.0 will need to settle this and document it in a \`# Stability\` section.

Risk for 0.0.0 / 0.1: low (no users yet). Risk if shipped at 1.0 with the current shape: every SCT-handling library in Rust depending on pkix-ct is locked to Vec for the life of the major version.
title: (api-contract) Public Vec fields on SctList, SignedCertificateTimestamp, MerkleAuditPath, SignedTreeHead lock in storage type forever
